'''Viatcheslav ("Slava") Borisovich Artaev''' (born January 24, 1960) is a Russian-American physicist who studies [[Mass spectrometry|Mass Spectrometry]] technology.  He currently works as the technical director for research and development of the separation science division for [[LECO Corporation]] based in [[St. Joseph, Michigan|Saint Joseph, Michigan, USA]].:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/viatcheslav-artaev-84aa4a5b/?challengeId=AQFG-9pJc7QOgQAAAW_NuoWifAIVfpbUyFh2cMCM3_iUJ_XrXtCiA0XerXnJfAH6ZkNiLKW4tjnLb0ixDdf86Mg82iiwcSd-Xg&submissionId=89609328-eb3c-ec15-6601-567c160c620b|title=Viatcheslav Artaev {{!}} LinkedIn|website=www.linkedin.com|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>

== Education ==
Artaev is a graduate of the Molecular Physics program at the [[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute)|Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] (MEPhI).<ref name="Facebook - Viatcheslav Artaev">{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/viatcheslav.artaev|title=Facebook - Viatcheslav Artaev}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Arrival in the United States and Meridian ===
Following the fall of the Soviet Union, Artaev sought to find work outside of the newly formed Russia due to concerns about political instability and the desire to build a better life for his family.  Ultimately, he was offered a temporary position  in [[Okemos, Michigan]] working for Meridian Instruments, a research and development group formed from [[Michigan State University]] graduates and professors. In 1993, Meridian offered Artaev a full-time position, and Artaev and his family immigrated to the [[United States]].   At Meridian Instruments, Artaev worked alongside computer programmer Kevin McNitt to develop the GC-TOFMS (Gas Chromatography [[Time-of-flight mass spectrometry|Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer]]), which could analyze a 60 compound VOC mixture in under 80 seconds, compared to the one hour for similar instruments available at the time.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/sponsored-content/mass-spectrometry-manchester-to-michigan/4010715.article|title=Mass spectrometry: Manchester to Michigan|last=Griffiths |first=Alan|date=2019-12-11 |website=Chemistry World|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>

=== LECO Corporation ===
In 1995, [[LECO Corporation]], which is based in [[St. Joseph, Michigan|Saint Joseph, Michigan]], acquired Artaev's project from Meridian Instruments and added Artaev and McNitt to their research and development team.  LECO heavily invested in continuing what Artaev and McNitt had developed at Meridian and eventually created the world's first commercial GC-TOFMS, known as the Pegasus, in 1997.<ref name=":0" /> The instrument was capable of recording in excess of 500 full spectra per second without data loss, something that many Mass Spectrometer manufacturers still struggle to accomplish to this day.<ref name=":0" />

Artaev put LECO on the forefront of cutting-edge technology in the Mass Spectrometry world.  Artaev continued to set scientific milestones by improving his Pegasus instrument to increase the speed and accuracy by which the instruments would produce data.  The instruments produced by LECO under Artaev's direction are<ref name=":0"/>

* 2002 Pegasus 4D – World's first GC×GC-TOFMS
* 2011 Pegasus GC-HRT – Accurate mass GC-TOFMS
* 2015 Pegasus GC-HRT 4D – World's first fast GC×GC accurate mass GC-TOFMS with up to 40m flight path
* 2016 Pegasus BT – Previous knowledge shrunk down to a bench-top, sensitivity and mass accuracy improved by orders of magnitude<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leco.com/product/pegasus-bt|title=Pegasus® BT GC-TOFMS|website=www.leco.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
* 2017 Pegasus GC-HRT<sup>+</sup> 4D – World's first full mass range fast accurate mass GC×GC-TOFMS<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leco.com/product/pegasus-gc-hrt-4d|title=Pegasus GC-HRT+ 4D|website=www.leco.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
* 2018 Pegasus BT 4D – World's first GC×GC TOFMS with quantitation spec as standard<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leco.com/product/pegasus-bt-4d|title=Pegasus® BT 4D GCxGC-TOFMS|website=www.leco.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>

In addition, Artaev is a founding member and former president of the Russian Mass Spectrometry Interest Group at [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry|ASMS]], which emerged in 1998 at the annual ASMS meeting in [[Orlando, Florida]]. The group was created to help assimilate mass spectrometrists from the former Soviet Union who were working the West. It has developed into a social and scientific club that now includes over 200 members. The interest group is notable not only for its work to assimilate scientists, but also for its impromptu musical performances around the hotel [[piano]], as well as [[water polo]] matches in the hotel pools.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://read.qxmd.com/read/31392702/the-russian-mass-spectrometry-interest-group-at-asms-over-20-years-of-science-and-water-polo|title=The Russian Mass Spectrometry Interest Group at ASMS: Over 20 Years of Science and Water Polo.|website=read.qxmd.com|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>

* A New Path to High-Resolution HPLC―TOF-MS — Survey, Targeted, and Trace Analysis Applications of TOF-MS in the Analysis of Complex Biochemical Matrices (2011)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chromatographyonline.com/new-path-high-resolution-hplc%E2%80%93tof-ms-%E2%80%94-survey-targeted-and-trace-analysis-applications-tof-ms-analys|title=Chromotography Online}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Viatcheslav has been married to Sabina Artaeva since 1984. Together they have two sons, both of whom are practicing attorneys in Michigan. In his spare time, Artaev enjoys travel to tropical destinations like [[Mexico]], and playing [[tennis]] and [[pickleball]].<ref name="Facebook - Viatcheslav Artaev"/>
